newsitem.title: UK: Investors snap up Brazil and Mexico mark bonds.
newsitem.headline: Investors snap up Brazil and Mexico mark bonds.

text.p: Investors on Tuesday rushed to buy 2.0 billion marks of bonds launched by Brazil and Mexico, two borrowers with rarity appeal, bankers said.
Both countries have nearly completed their international funding for 1997, and when they return to the market next year the yield pick-up for emerging market debt could be much lower.
"Mexico has said this is its last (1997) deal in a leading currency," an official at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, underwriter of Mexico's Eurobond said.
"The view on Latin American countries is very positive. So in future they may issue at much tighter spreads. Investors saw this as a last chance to get hold of paper which offered yield."
Brazil set a 500 million mark 10-year bond and was quickly followed by a 1.5 billion mark 12-year issue from Mexico.
Brazil -- rated B1 by Moody's and B by Standard & Poor's -- paid 2.3 percentage points over Bunds and Mexico -- rated Ba2/BB -- offered a 2.6 point yield pick-up.
When Latin American countries first started issuing 10-year mark bonds in March last year, they offered nearly five percentage points over Bunds.
Since the start of this year spreads on emerging market mark Eurobonds have come another 30 to 40 basis points, dealers said.

"There is so much demand now for high-yielding products. The sector is hot, not just in marks but in all currencies," a syndicate manager at Credit Suisse First Boston, which brought the Brazil bond said.
Institutional investors bought around half of the Mexico deal, the first time they have been heavy buyers of an emerging market mark Eurobond, the Deutsche official said.
"We sold out of the Mexico bond at the time of the launch," the Deutsche Morgan Grenfell official said.
"It was a big, big success. We were surprised by the strong demand and it shows there is a huge appetite for high-yield products in marks," he said.
Today's deals will likely be the last for some time from both Brazil and Mexico.
Mexico raised most of its international funding requirements for 1997 in January. Brazil has quite meagre international borrowing needs.
Bankers in Mexico said on Monday the proceeds of the mark bond may be used to buy-back outstanding Brady bonds.
A few more jumbo emerging market bonds were expected in marks in the coming months.
Argentina may issue a 1.5 billion mark bond later in February. It could tap the 30-year maturity, as it did last year, or even extend its yield curve in marks.
Russia said on Monday it planned to issue a 1.0 billion mark bond in March, its second international bond issue. The deal is expected to have a seven-year maturity.
"In general, the reception of today's deals is good news for all emerging market paper and we expect Russia will take full advantage of that," the Deutsche official said.
